Abstract

War for Eternity, by Benjamin Teitelbaum, is the account of his search for the understanding of Traditionalism, an extreme-right current of thought, through dialogues with its main current exponents. His proposal was to understand how such radical ideals, which have always been on the sidelines of public debate, have gained importance in recent years, coming to influence political leaders in several countries. For this, Teitelbaum attended events linked to Traditionalist circles and interviewed some of their representatives, giving special attention to those who became ideological gurus for the presidents of three countries: Brazil, United States and Russia, which, at the time of the reports, were commanded by Jair Bolsonaro, Donald Trump, and Vladimir Putin, respectively. It is an essential work to understand the most transformative political movement of the beginning of the 21st century.

# Benjamin Teitelbaum, PhD '13, Earns Tenure at University of Colorado Boulder

Benjamin Teitelbaum The Department of Music is proud to share the news that Benjamin Teitelbaum (PhD '13, Ethnomusicology) received tenure and the rank of Associate Professor of Musicology and International Affairs at the University of Colorado Boulder. Teitelbaum joined Colorado's Musicology department in 2017, and since published the monographs _Lions of the North: Sounds of the New Nordic Radical Nationalism_ (Oxford UP 2017) and _War for Eternity: The Return of Traditionalism and the Rise of the Populist Right_ (Penguin 2020) in addition to academic articles, chapters, and features and op-eds in _The New York Times_ , the _Wall Street Journal_ , _The Nation_ , and _The Atlantic_ . Congratulations, Dr. Teitelbaum!
